title: Washing Machine Plumbing: Copper Pipe Connections, Fluxing, and Stainless Braided Hoses (This Old House)
summary: This Old House demonstrates a practical laundry-room plumbing upgrade, starting with a small carpentry box and bell-shaped pipe hangers to support copper supply lines. The presenter routes hot and cold feeds to a dedicated washing-machine valve, then cuts, cleans, fluxes, and solder-fits copper pipe and fittings, including a tee to feed the new washer connection. The assembly is completed by replacing aging rubber hoses with stainless steel braided supply hoses and testing the water supply by opening the cold and hot valves. The segment emphasizes careful fluxing, conservative solder usage to protect fittings, and proper valve operation to relieve pressure when away from home.

sections.title: Carpentry box and bell hangers
sections.description: Build a box with a plate at the top and bottom and install studs on the sides; secure the assembly with screws. Plan to mount copper pipe using bell-shaped hangers, which are clipped to hold the pipe.

sections.title: Plan, hot/cold lines, and washing machine valve
sections.description: Identify hot and cold lines, bring them down to the new washing-machine valve, and note that the valve has an off/on position to relieve pressure when away from home.

sections.title: Copper pipe prep: cut, clean, flux
sections.description: Cut pipe pieces, clean the outside of the pipe, clean the inside of fittings with a brush, and apply flux in preparation for soldering.

sections.title: Soldering and final assembly
sections.description: Heat the joint and let solder flow into the fitting; use minimal solder to avoid damaging the fitting, then proceed to assemble the rest of the connections.

sections.title: Final test: hose upgrade and valve operation
sections.description: Replace old single-wall hoses with stainless steel braided hoses, connect the washing-machine supply, and open the cold and hot valves to verify the setup and demonstrate that the washer is ready for use.
